Connect the $340 \text{ m}^3$ per minute flow to mass per second using density $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and division by $60 \text{ s}$.

walkthrough: Identify the energy source: water of mass $m$ dropping height $h = 30 \text{ m}$ loses $mgh$ of gravitational potential energy per unit time.
Find mass passing per second. Volume rate is $340/60 \approx 5.67 \text{ m}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$, so mass rate is $\rho V/t = 1000 \times 5.67 \approx 5.67 \times 10^3 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$.
